title: Blowups on a projective scheme over an affine Noetherian base are H-projective
statement: Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a commutative Noetherian ring $A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $f:X\to S$ be H-projective, meaning that it factors as a closed immersion into some finite-dimensional projective space $\mathbf P^N_S$ followed by projection [def-kun-projective] [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For any finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [pqf-def-coherent], the ordinary blowup $b:B=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X\to X$ [def-nagata-global-blowup] is H-projective, and so is $f b:B\to S$. The empty blowup for $\mathcal I=0$ and the identity blowup for $\mathcal I=\mathcal O_X$ are allowed. No integrality, regularity or excellence hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 02NS (lemma-blowing-up-projective), combined with morphisms.tex Tag 087S (lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective) and Tag 01WE (lemma-H-projective-composition); an H-projective scheme over an affine base has an ample invertible sheaf by Tag 01VR/01VG and absolute ampleness over an affine base.

proof.text: Choose the factorization $X\xrightarrow{i}\mathbf P^N_S\xrightarrow{q}S$ in [def-kun-projective]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ample-invertible] with the given ring $A$, this $N$, and this closed immersion $i$. Its statement supplies an invertible sheaf $\mathcal L=i^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^N_A}(1)$ which is ample on $X$ in the absolute sense. Thus the base $X$ of the blowup admits exactly the ample invertible sheaf required later; no passage from relative to absolute ampleness is left implicit.

source.place: Tags 01PS (definition-ample), 01PU (lemma-ample-on-closed), together with Constructions Tag 01NG (lemma-standard-covering-projective-space); the existing projective-ample node gives the absolute affine-base conclusion

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-rees-symmetric-presentation] to $X,\mathcal I$. It supplies the quasi-coherent graded algebra $\mathcal R$, the restriction-compatible affine Rees identifications $\theta_V$ (identity in degree zero), and the degreewise surjective graded morphism $\varphi:\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal I)\to\mathcal R$. Since $\mathcal I$ is of finite type, all hypotheses of [lem-sfb-rees-presentation-blowup-immersion] hold with $\mathcal C=\mathcal R$. Its closed immersion $j:B\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_X(\mathcal I)$ is over $X$ and has composite $b$. Taking $\mathcal E=\mathcal I$ in [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] proves that $b$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense.

source.place: Tag 02NS (lemma-blowing-up-projective), proof of clause (1): assembly of the graded presentation and chart-compatible closed immersion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective] to $b:B\to X$. Step 2 supplies its projective-bundle hypothesis, and Step 1 supplies an ample invertible sheaf on its base $X$. Therefore $b$ is H-projective in the finite-projective-space convention of the item. In particular this step uses no integrality or nonzero-ideal hypothesis.

The given $f:X\to S$ is H-projective, and Step 3 proves the same for $b$. Apply [lem-trf-h-projective-composition] with $g=b$ and $h=f$ to obtain that $fb:B\to S$ is H-projective as well. All steps apply to every finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, including $0$ and $\mathcal O_X$, and to an empty $X$. The argument has imposed no additional hypothesis on $X$ or $A$.
